nodes.label: The project banner
nodes.rationale: A 1200x320 hand-authored SVG banner on a near-black vertical gradient with a soft radial light pool at upper right. Left half: the red bolt mark at 2.55x scale, the wordmark 'Catalyst' in heavy white beside 'Console' in light grey, a one-line strapline, and a red-to-transparent sweep rule under it. Right half: a suggested dashboard. Not a photograph or a screenshot — the whole thing is drawn in primitives so it stays a few kilobytes and renders under the same no-network constraint the app itself works under.

nodes.label: The board, suggested rather than drawn
nodes.rationale: Six rounded dark rectangles at 50% opacity stand in for tiles, with one blue trace polyline, one green gauge arc on a grey track, and two progress bars — one red, one amber. Enough to read as instruments without being a legible screenshot: this is a dashboard of tiles, and that is the one thing a banner should say before any words do.

nodes.label: The three rules set in monospace on the banner
nodes.rationale: Three numbered monospace lines at the foot of the left column — 01 It never controls the robot, 02 Nothing it does may impede driving, 03 It never invents a number — set in a dim grey rather than the headline white. The source comment says why they are there at all: 'The three rules, because they are the product.' The rules appear in the marketing artwork, the README, the docs index and the running About panel, which is four independent restatements of the same three sentences.

nodes.label: The console's own palette
nodes.rationale: Catalyst red #e94560 for the mark and the sweep, near-black grounds #16171b to #0a0b0d, grey #9a9ba1 for secondary text, with status colours quoted in the mock tiles: blue #4d90fe for a trace, green #30d158 for a healthy gauge, amber #ff9f0a for a warning bar. The source calls the ground 'The console's own ground, not the library's. Siblings rather than copies' — deliberately adjacent to FrcCatalyst's identity without being derived from it.
